title: International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC), Revision 5
supports: ISIC is the international economic-activity reference classification
Revision 5 was endorsed by the UN Statistical Commission
Revision 5 structure and explanatory notes are available while the formal publication remains forthcoming
limitations: Landing-page path retains /4 although the page now presents Revision 5
Formal publication is described as forthcoming

title: ISIC Revision 5 English structure (CSV)
supports: Complete official code-and-title hierarchy for ISIC Revision 5
22 sections, 87 divisions, 258 groups and 463 classes
limitations: Structure file does not itself carry explanatory notes or assignment examples

title: ISIC Revision 4 classification registry record
supports: ISIC classifies economic activities
Revision 4 hierarchy has 21 sections, 88 divisions, 238 groups and 419 classes
Official cross-classification correspondence tables exist
authority_scope: Global economic-activity classification and correspondence metadata
limitations: Revision 4 is no longer the newest ISIC edition

title: Technical Note on the ISIC Rev. 4–Rev. 5 Correspondence Table
supports: Official correspondence between ISIC Revision 4 and Revision 5 requires documented code formats and interpretation
limitations: A correspondence is not proof of lossless equivalence for every code

title: Best Practice Guidelines for Developing International Statistical Classifications
publisher: United Nations Committee of Experts on International Statistical Classifications
supports: Classification categories require logical codes and clear descriptors
Explanatory notes should clarify inclusions, exclusions and boundaries
Classification maintenance, review and versioning are governed activities
authority_scope: Development and maintenance of international statistical classifications
limitations: Guidance does not select an enterprise product taxonomy

title: UNSD International Family of Classifications by statistical domain
supports: Industry classification is one graph among product, purpose, provider, energy, transport and other statistical classifications
Specialist classifications are needed alongside ISIC
authority_scope: Global inventory of official statistical classifications
limitations: Registry presence does not make two classifications semantically interchangeable

title: Central Product Classification Version 3.0
supports: CPC classifies goods and services rather than industries
CPC Version 3.0 was adopted in 2025
limitations: Product categories must not be substituted for economic-activity categories

title: North American Industry Classification System
supports: NAICS is the U.S. federal statistical standard for business establishments
NAICS is jointly developed for North American comparability
Official manuals, files and concordances are published
limitations: Administrative uses do not change its production-oriented statistical design
A 2027 revision process is under way

title: 2022 North American Industry Classification System Manual
supports: 2022 NAICS United States covers all economic activities with 20 sectors and 1,012 U.S. industries
NAICS groups establishments by similarity of production processes
limitations: National detail and codes are edition-specific

title: NAICS Canada 2022 Version 1.0
supports: NAICS Canada 2022 contains 20 sectors through 923 Canadian industries
Official structure files and an ISIC Revision 4 correspondence are published
Statistics Canada publishes specialist variants for energy, ICT, content and media, labour force and other analytical views
limitations: Canadian national detail is not automatically interchangeable with U.S. or Mexican detail

title: Sistema de Clasificación Industrial de América del Norte, México SCIAN 2023
publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía
supports: SCIAN México 2023 is Mexico's current North American industrial classification
Trilateral changes and national-detail changes are separately described
limitations: National detail differs even where trilateral levels are comparable
Primary publication is in Spanish

title: NACE Revision 2 Update 1 overview
supports: NACE Rev. 2.1 is the newest EU economic-activity classification
NACE Rev. 2.1 is used for European statistics from 2025 onward
Transition requires correspondence, backcasting and double reporting
limitations: Historical European statistics may remain on NACE Rev. 2

title: NACE Rev. 2.1 – Statistical classification of economic activities in the European Union – 2025 edition
supports: NACE classification use requires methodological guidance and explanatory notes
limitations: Manual applies to the EU classification, not every national extension

title: Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification 2006 Revision 2.0
publisher: Australian Bureau of Statistics and Statistics New Zealand
supports: ANZSIC supports industry statistics in Australia and New Zealand
Revision 2.0 preserves structure while clarifying emerging activities and definitions
ANZSIC was aligned as far as possible with ISIC Revision 4
authority_scope: Australia and New Zealand economic-activity classification
limitations: Alignment as far as possible is not identity with ISIC

title: UK Standard Industrial Classification 2026
supports: UK SIC 2026 structure, notes, index and 2007 correspondence were published in August 2026
The framework classifies establishments and other statistical units by economic activity
limitations: Operational adoption is phased; earliest anticipated National Accounts use is 2031

title: Singapore Standard Industrial Classification 2025
supports: SSIC 2025 is Singapore's national economic-activity standard
SSIC 2025 adopts the ISIC Revision 5 framework with national modifications
Official SSIC 2025 to ISIC Revision 5 and SSIC 2020 correspondence tables are published
limitations: National modifications prevent assuming code identity with ISIC

title: National Industrial Classification 2008 code finder and files
publisher: Government of India Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
supports: NIC 2008 is India's published economic-activity classification
Official code finder, corrigendum and Excel structure are available
limitations: NIC 2008 is based on ISIC Revision 4 and may not represent later structural changes

title: Singapore Standard Industrial Classification 2025 report
supports: Economic activity, principal activity and value-added assignment concepts are explicitly defined
The production boundary derives from the System of National Accounts
New national codes cover emerging activities
limitations: Singapore-specific modifications must be retained in crosswalks

title: International Standard Classification of Education 2011
supports: ISCED classifies education programmes and qualifications by internationally agreed levels
Education level is distinct from provider economic activity
limitations: ISCED levels are not an industry hierarchy

title: ISCED Fields of Education and Training 2013
supports: Fields of education and levels of education are independent cross-classification variables
ISCED-F has broad, narrow and detailed field levels
authority_scope: Global classification of education and training fields
limitations: Fields of study must not be modeled as education-provider subindustries

title: A System of Health Accounts 2011 Revised Edition
publisher: OECD, European Union and World Health Organization
supports: Health analysis distinguishes provider, function and financing classifications
ICHA-HP includes hospitals, long-term care, ambulatory care, ancillary services, retailers, prevention and administration
limitations: Health-account provider categories are not identical to general economic-activity classes

title: International Recommendations for Tourism Statistics 2008
publisher: United Nations Statistics Division and World Tourism Organization
supports: Tourism industries are derived from visitor-related characteristic activities rather than a single ordinary industry branch
Tourism analysis crosses activity, product, trip and visitor classifications
authority_scope: Global tourism statistics and tourism-industry overlay
limitations: Tourism characteristic status depends on visitor demand and cannot be inferred from an establishment code alone

title: List of categories of tourism characteristic activities (tourism industries)
publisher: United Nations Statistics Division and World Tourism Organization
supports: The official tourism-industry overlay contains 12 categories
The overlay maps to ISIC Revision 4 and is used for Tourism Satellite Accounts
limitations: The 2008 overlay requires edition-aware migration before use with ISIC Revision 5

title: Indicative Crop Classification 1.1
publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
supports: ICC is the FAO-custodied crop classification for the World Programme for the Census of Agriculture
Official classifications and correspondences are machine-accessible
limitations: A crop classification describes crop kinds, not all agricultural industries or farm business models

title: Standard International Energy Products Classification
supports: SIEC classifies energy products across production, transformation and consumption
SIEC Version 1 was endorsed in 2011 as part of IRES
The custodian publishes Version 2 structure and revision materials
limitations: The landing-page revision narrative still describes Version 2 as draft; the later 57th-session decision is authoritative for its March 2026 endorsement status

title: Report on the fifty-seventh session of the United Nations Statistical Commission — Decision 57/121
supports: The Commission endorsed the structure of SIEC Version 2.0 as an international statistical classification in March 2026
The Commission requested finalization of explanatory notes and relevant correspondences
authority_scope: Formal adoption status of international statistical classifications at the 57th session
limitations: The decision endorses the structure while explicitly leaving explanatory notes and correspondences to be finalized

title: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting 2012 Central Framework
supports: Environmental activities include environmental protection and resource-management classifications
Environmental activity views cut across ordinary economic-activity industries
authority_scope: Global environmental-economic accounting and Classification of Environmental Activities
limitations: Ongoing classification updates require explicit edition status

title: Harmonized System Nomenclature 2022 Edition
supports: HS 2022 is the global customs nomenclature for traded goods
Official 2017-to-2022 correlation tables are published
authority_scope: International merchandise classification under the HS Convention
limitations: HS goods codes are not industries and national tariff schedules add jurisdictional detail
Correlation tables are implementation aids, not universal classification rulings

title: OECD Handbook on Compiling Digital Supply and Use Tables — Digital industries
publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
supports: Digital industries are overlays on established ISIC categories rather than a new exhaustive industry tree
The ICT-sector definition spans manufacturing, trade and service activity codes
limitations: The ICT sector is narrower than the digital economy and country implementations may vary

title: Classification of the Functions of Government
supports: COFOG classifies government functions and socioeconomic objectives
The operational 1999 classification is under revision with completion anticipated in 2028
limitations: Government function is not the same axis as public-sector industry
Revision work is not yet an endorsed replacement

title: International Classification of Non-Profit Organizations
supports: ICNPO provides specialist detail for nonprofit institutions
ICNPO builds on but is not identical to the ISIC activity classification
limitations: The operational edition is based on ISIC Revision 3 and needs edition-aware mapping

title: Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience — 16 Critical Infrastructure Sectors
supports: Critical-infrastructure sectors are a criticality and resilience overlay
The U.S. framework contains 16 interconnected sectors
authority_scope: United States critical-infrastructure security and resilience
limitations: Criticality sectors are jurisdiction-specific and do not replace economic-activity classifications

title: Economics: National Ocean Watch
supports: The marine economy is a cross-industry overlay with an explicit sectors-and-industries crosswalk
ENOW publishes scope, source data, time coverage and limitations
authority_scope: United States ocean- and Great-Lakes-dependent economic activity
limitations: U.S.-specific geography and imputation methods limit global equivalence
Open ENOW is less detailed than the original employer-microdata series

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement lines of business
supports: Insurance regulatory analysis uses lines of business distinct from insurer industry codes
Line-specific data definitions and annual evolution are governed
authority_scope: United States state insurance market-conduct reporting
limitations: MCAS lines are a regulatory reporting overlay, not a global insurance-industry taxonomy

title: GSIM Statistical Classifications Model
publisher: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe
supports: A statistical classification is a maintained scheme of categories assignable to variables
Classification series, classifications and items require separate identities
limitations: GSIM is a metamodel and does not supply industry content

title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
supports: Cross-scheme mappings distinguish exact, close, broad, narrow and related matches
Exact match has stronger and transitive semantics than close match
limitations: Industry crosswalk cardinality, statistical units and allocation loss require extensions beyond SKOS

title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
supports: Evidence provenance distinguishes entities, activities and responsible agents
Qualified attribution, derivation, revision and primary-source relations can carry provenance details
limitations: PROV-O does not define classification-quality thresholds

title: SDMX 2.1 Information Model
supports: Codes, codelists, concept schemes and data/metadata structures are distinct model objects
Complex classification associations may exceed a simple codelist
authority_scope: Exchange of statistical data and metadata
limitations: SDMX transport structures do not prove semantic equivalence between industry codes

title: NAICS concordances and downloadable reference files
supports: Official NAICS concordances are published separately from classification structures
Edition-to-edition and external-classification bridges must identify their exact source and target editions
limitations: Concordance rows can be many-to-many and are not universal entity recodes

title: NACE correspondence tables
supports: NACE revision migration is published as correspondence tables
Crosswalk use must retain source and target edition direction
limitations: Correspondence does not by itself preserve time-series values; backcasting may be required

title: ISIC Revision 4 class 7210 classification detail
supports: A usable classification node includes hierarchy, explanatory notes, inclusions and correspondence
Product correspondence may be one-to-many
limitations: One class is an implementation example, not evidence for every class boundary

title: International Recommendations for Energy Statistics
supports: Energy statistics require product, flow, producer and consumer distinctions
SIEC categories are designed to be exhaustive and mutually exclusive within their product scope
limitations: Energy-product exhaustiveness does not imply industry-activity exhaustiveness

title: Key classifications of the System of Health Accounts 2011
publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
supports: Health functions, providers and financing schemes are separately enumerated
Healthcare analysis requires cross-classification rather than a single provider tree
authority_scope: Operational presentation of SHA health classifications
limitations: Health accounts do not enumerate clinical specialties, diagnoses or interventions completely

title: FAO agriculture data collection and classifications
publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
supports: Agricultural statistics cross crop, livestock, commodity, land, input and environmental classifications
Commodity correspondences link FAO lists, CPC and HS
authority_scope: Global food and agriculture statistical collection
limitations: Collection classifications are multiple orthogonal axes, not one subindustry hierarchy
